partners.mechanism_chain: LAMP2 (HGNC:6576) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal autophagic degradation (GO:0000283); lysosomal autophagic degradation (GO:0000283) —LEADS_TO→ cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); APOA1 (HGNC:704) —DISRUPTS→ APOA1 amyloid fibril (CHEBI:773); APOA1 amyloid fibril (CHEBI:773) —LEADS_TO→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ amyloidosis (HP:0003230); lysosomal autophagic degradation (GO:0000283) —DECREASES→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198). Loss-of-function mutations in LAMP2 disrupt lysosomal autophagic degradation, leading to cardiomyopathy in Danon disease. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in APOA1 lead to the formation of APOA1 amyloid fibrils, which impair extracellular matrix organization and cause amyloidosis. The disruption of lysosomal function by LAMP2 deficiency can secondarily impair extracellular matrix organization, creating a convergence point.

raw.translational: Understanding potential overlaps in cellular mechanisms between seemingly disparate diseases like Danon disease and Glanzmann thrombasthenia could reveal novel therapeutic targets. #### 1. amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608)

**Proposed mechanism:** LAMP2 (HGNC:6576) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal autophagic degradation (GO:0000283); lysosomal autophagic degradation (GO:0000283) —LEADS_TO→ cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); APOA1 (HGNC:704) —DISRUPTS→ APOA1 amyloid fibril (CHEBI:773); APOA1 amyloid fibril (CHEBI:773) —LEADS_TO→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ amyloidosis (HP:0003230); lysosomal autophagic degradation (GO:0000283) —DECREASES→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198). Loss-of-function mutations in LAMP2 disrupt lysosomal autophagic degradation, leading to cardiomyopathy in Danon disease. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in APOA1 lead to the formation of APOA1 amyloid fibrils, which impair extracellular matrix organization and cause amyloidosis. The disruption of lysosomal function by LAMP2 deficiency can secondarily impair extracellular matrix organization, creating a convergence point.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any observed cardiac abnormalities or amyloid deposition in individuals with documented loss-of-function mutations in LAMP2 or APOA1, respectively, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Any common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.01) in either LAMP2 or APOA1 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic links between lysosomal dysfunction and extracellular matrix integrity in Danon disease and amyloidosis could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both conditions, potentially involving modulation of autophagy or extracellular matrix remodeling pathways.

#### 2. Glanzmann thrombasthenia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.405)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608)

**Proposed mechanism:** LAMP2 (HGNC:6522) —DISRUPTS→ Autophagosome-lysosome fusion and degradation (GO:0005777); Autophagosome-lysosome fusion and degradation (GO:0005777) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); ITGA2B (HGNC:5685) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0001753); ITGB3 (HGNC:5682) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0001753); Platelet activation and aggregation (GO:0001753) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001892). Mutations in LAMP2 lead to impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion and degradation, contributing to cardiomyopathy. Mutations in ITGA2B and ITGB3 disrupt the integrin alpha-IIb beta-3 complex, impairing platelet activation and aggregation, leading to bleeding. The mechanistic overlap is hypothesized to be at the level of cellular signaling pathways that are affected by general cellular stress or protein turnover issues, potentially influencing downstream processes common to both cell types (e.g., cellular integrity maintenance), although the primary molecular defects are distinct.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies show that mutations in LAMP2 do not lead to any detectable downstream effects on cellular adhesion or signaling pathways, or if mutations in ITGA2B/ITGB3 do not impact general cellular processes beyond platelet function, the proposed mechanistic link would be falsified. Specifically, if no shared downstream cellular pathways or processes can be experimentally demonstrated to be affected by defects in both LAMP2 and ITGA2B/ITGB3, the hypothesis is weakened. _(variant: gnomad.broadinstitute.org/variant/GRCh38/11/52202421-52202421-C-T)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding potential overlaps in cellular mechanisms between seemingly disparate diseases like Danon disease and Glanzmann thrombasthenia could reveal novel therapeutic targets. For example, if lysosomal dysfunction in Danon disease exacerbates cellular stress that impairs integrin function in other cell types, or if impaired platelet function due to Glanzmann thrombasthenia leads to secondary cellular damage that is influenced by lysosomal pathways, therapies targeting these shared pathways could offer a broader benefit.
